name: The Rise and Potential of Large Language Model Based Agents: A Survey (LLM-Agent Survey / Xi et al.)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2309.07864, cs.AI/cs.CL); submitted 14 Sep 2023, v3 19 Sep 2023, 86 pages. Later formally published (peer-reviewed) as a REVIEW in Science China Information Sciences (SCIS), Feb 2025, Vol. 68, Iss. 2, 121101 (44 pages), DOI 10.1007/s11432-024-4222-0 (received 7 Sep 2024 / accepted 11 Nov 2024 / published online 17 Jan 2025).
authors_affiliation: Zhiheng Xi, Wenxiang Chen, Xin Guo, Wei He, Yiwen Ding, Boyang Hong, Ming Zhang, Junzhe Wang, Senjie Jin, Enyu Zhou (10 co-first authors), Rui Zheng, ... Xipeng Qiu, Xuanjing Huang, Qi Zhang (corresponding) and Tao Gui (corresponding), et al. (29 authors). Primary affiliation: School of Computer Science, Fudan University, Shanghai, China (with Fudan College of Foreign Languages & Literature, Institute of Modern Languages and Linguistics, and Meituan).
code_url: https://github.com/WooooDyy/LLM-Agent-Paper-List (curated paper list / reading list accompanying the survey; not a runnable method implementation since this is a survey).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/WooooDyy/LLM-Agent-Paper-List (continuously-updated GitHub paper list maintained by the authors; describes itself as the paper list of the 86-page SCIS cover paper).
task_domain: Survey / taxonomy. Broad survey of LLM-based agents spanning planning, tool-use, embodied, web, multi-agent, decision-making, and human-agent cooperation; not restricted to a single task domain.
problem_setting: This is a comprehensive literature survey (not a method/system with experiments). It traces the concept of agents from philosophical origins to AI, argues why LLMs are suitable agent foundations, and proposes a conceptual framework for LLM-based agents with three components: brain, perception, and action. It then organizes applications into single-agent scenarios, multi-agent scenarios, and human-agent cooperation, and discusses agent society (behavior/personality, emergent social phenomena) and open problems. It covers both offline and interactive settings and both single- and multi-agent systems as surveyed sub-areas, but the survey itself defines no controlled experimental protocol, supervision, or benchmark of its own.
what_is_retrieved: N/A for the survey as an artifact (it does not itself retrieve). As a surveyed topic, it covers agent memory retrieval (retrieving past experiences/dialogue history/observations from agent memory) and tool-related knowledge (tool descriptions/manuals, demonstrations). The brain module discussion includes knowledge, memory (recall of prior interactions), and tool descriptions as content an agent draws upon.
retrieval_grounding: Survey-level: covers BOTH a GROWING/episodic agent memory (the surveyed 'memory capability' where agents store and later retrieve past interactions/experiences) and access to STATIC external knowledge/tools (knowledge, tool manuals/APIs). The survey itself is not grounded in any single corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: N/A (survey, no retrieval objective of its own). The surveyed memory-retrieval discussion describes top-scoring selection via a weighted recency+relevance+importance memory score (i.e., a ranked top-k style selection in the generative-agents line it cites), not a completeness objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (the survey is not a case-based reasoning system; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle is implemented).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The survey does not frame LLM-based agents as case-based reasoning and does not center Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it organizes the field around a brain/perception/action framework (with memory, knowledge, reasoning/planning, tool-use, etc.).
retrieval_unit: N/A (survey defines no retrieval unit of its own). Surveyed memory units include past dialogue/interaction history and stored experiences/observations (episodic memory entries); surveyed tool-use units include tool descriptions/manuals and usage demonstrations.
index_source: N/A for the survey. Surveyed memory is a growing store that agents write during interaction (online/test-time-induced episodic memory); surveyed tool/knowledge access is from static external resources. The survey itself builds no index.
index_structure_topology: N/A (survey has no index of its own). It reviews memory storage substrates used by agents (e.g., natural-language memory in context, external vector/embedding stores, and structured databases such as SQL/ChatDB/DB-GPT), i.e., it surveys both flat and structured/database memory organizations rather than prescribing one.
retriever_type: N/A (survey; no retriever implemented). The surveyed memory-retrieval methods include embedding/similarity-based retrieval plus heuristic scoring (recency/relevance/importance weighting), and database-query retrieval (SQL). Tool selection is described as LLM-driven (prompt/feedback based).
retriever_learning_signal: N/A (survey; no retriever is trained). It surveys agents that learn tool use from zero-shot/few-shot prompts and from environmental/human feedback, and memory retrieval driven by hand-designed scoring (recency+relevance+importance) rather than a trained retriever.
query_construction: N/A (survey). For surveyed memory retrieval, the current interaction/state acts as the query that is matched against stored memories; no query-construction method is proposed by the survey itself.
query_granularity: N/A (survey). Surveyed agents retrieve from memory at the step/interaction level during a task (when the agent needs relevant content to make a decision), but the survey prescribes no single granularity.
when_to_retrieve: N/A (survey). Surveyed memory retrieval occurs interactively (when the agent must access relevant memory content to make a decision during environment interaction); the survey does not standardize a trigger.
retrieval_trigger_signal: N/A (survey defines no trigger). Surveyed agent-initiated retrieval is driven by the agent's need for relevant memory during decision-making (agent-initiated / per-interaction), and tool invocation is agent-initiated within reasoning loops.
reranking: N/A (survey; no reranking stage of its own). It notes memory-score-based prioritization (weighted recency/relevance/importance) as a selection/ranking heuristic in the generative-agents line it cites.
retrieved_context_refinement: N/A (survey). It discusses memory reflection/summarization (e.g., summarizing or editing dialogue history, interactive memory objects that can be moved/edited/deleted/combined via summarization) as post-storage processing in surveyed systems, but proposes no refinement pipeline itself.
tool_document_engineering: Surveyed (not a method contribution): the survey describes agents learning tools via zero-shot prompts containing tool functionality and parameter descriptions and few-shot prompts providing usage demonstrations (analogous to consulting tool manuals or observing usage), plus learning tools from environmental and human feedback. It does not propose its own tool-document-engineering technique.
index_content_separation: N/A (survey; no index-vs-content separation mechanism of its own).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (survey). It predates and does not cover MCP; it surveys tool use via prompting/API-calling and feedback-based learning rather than a live-synchronized tool index/protocol.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (survey). It discusses single-tool and multi-tool use and tool-creation/learning at a high level but does not center an inter-tool dependency-graph retrieval formalism.
how_retrieved_used: N/A as a method. The survey describes how agents use retrieved/recalled content: prompt augmentation (recalled memory and tool descriptions/demos placed in the LLM context to inform reasoning, planning, and action), tool invocation, and reflection. No method is implemented by the survey.
planning_integration: N/A as a method. The survey reviews planning as a brain/reasoning capability with two stages: plan formulation (decompose an overarching task into sub-tasks) and plan reflection. It catalogs planning-without-feedback styles (single-step full-plan-then-execute; adaptive CoT-series one-sub-task-at-a-time; hierarchical planning; tree-structured search over candidate paths) and planning-with-feedback (environment/human/model feedback), but proposes no single integration.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: N/A (survey). It contrasts decompose-first (one-shot full plan) vs adaptive/interleaved per-step planning (CoT-series, ReAct-style) as surveyed paradigms rather than committing to one interleaving granularity.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method; no retrieved-case adaptation mechanism of its own).
retrieved_item_representation: N/A (survey). Surveyed memory/knowledge is mostly represented as natural-language (free-text) entries (past interactions, observations, reflections) or stored in databases; the survey injects nothing itself.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: N/A (survey). Surveyed memory ranges from raw interaction/dialogue history to distilled/summarized reflections; the survey reviews this spectrum rather than fixing an abstraction level.
noise_robustness_mechanism: N/A (survey). It discusses memory reflection/summarization and feedback-driven correction in surveyed agents and notes general robustness/hallucination challenges, but contributes no specific noise-robustness mechanism.
memory_type: Survey-level: the brain/perception/action framework explicitly includes a Memory capability (episodic agent memory of past interactions/experiences), alongside knowledge. It reviews short-term (in-context) and long-term memory and various storage substrates (natural language, embeddings/vector stores, structured databases). As an artifact the survey itself has no memory.
write_back: N/A as a method. Surveyed agents DO write back experiences/dialogue into memory (the memory capability stores past interactions for later retrieval), and the survey covers memory reading, writing, and reflection as core operations; but the survey itself stores nothing.
online_growth: N/A as a method. Surveyed agent memory grows online during interaction/deployment (the agent continually stores new interactions/experiences); the survey itself has no growing store.
write_back_trigger: N/A (survey; no write-back trigger of its own). Surveyed memory writing is generally per-interaction / per-step during environment interaction, with reflective summarization/editing of stored memory in some cited systems; the survey does not standardize a trigger.
failure_experience_usage: N/A (survey). It discusses agents learning from environmental feedback (including whether actions succeeded or failed) and self-reflection, implying use of both success and failure signals in surveyed systems, but contributes no specific failure-experience storage scheme.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (survey). It notes memory operations such as editing, deleting, combining via summarization, and reflection (i.e., post-write mutation in cited systems like interactive memory objects, ChatDB/DB-GPT SQL deletion), but proposes no single update policy.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: N/A (survey). Surveyed memory retrieval is largely heuristic (recency/relevance/importance scoring) or similarity/database-query based, not a learned RL retrieval policy; the survey does not center retrieval-as-learned-policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Surveyed (not a method contribution): the survey devotes major sections to multi-agent scenarios (cooperative and adversarial), agent communication, and agent societies, which include shared/collective information and experience across multiple agents; it reviews rather than implements cross-agent sharing.
benchmarks: N/A (survey; runs no experiments and reports no benchmark results of its own). It references and discusses many agent benchmarks/environments used by surveyed works (e.g., embodied/game environments, web/tool/QA settings) but presents no controlled evaluation.
benchmark_family: N/A (survey). Surveyed sub-areas span embodied (e.g., Minecraft/Voyager-style, ALFWorld-type), web, tool-use, QA, code, and multi-agent/social-simulation families, but the survey itself reports no benchmark family results.
baselines: N/A (survey; no method comparison or baselines of its own).
key_metrics: N/A (survey; reports no quantitative metrics of its own).
headline_result: N/A (survey; no headline number). Its 'headline' contribution is the conceptual brain/perception/action framework for LLM-based agents plus a comprehensive, widely-cited organization of the field (highly cited: >1,700 citations on the arXiv version; the SCIS journal version reports 512 references).
ablations: N/A (survey; no ablations). As a literature survey it conducts no experiments and therefore reports no component ablations.
evaluation_decoupling: N/A (survey reports no retrieval or end-to-end metrics). It does include a dedicated discussion of evaluating LLM-based agents (utility, sociability, values, etc.) as an open topic, but no intrinsic-vs-end-to-end metric decoupling is performed.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: N/A (survey; performs no scoring). It discusses, at the field level, evaluation dimensions for agents (capabilities and behaviors) but does not itself score process or outcome.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: N/A (survey; no cost/efficiency measurements of its own). Efficiency/cost of agents is mentioned only as a general discussion topic.
context_budget_and_selection_count: N/A (survey; no token budget or k of its own). It discusses agents' limited context windows and the role of memory in extending effective context as a surveyed challenge.
survey_scope_and_axes: Primary organizing axes: (1) a general LLM-based-agent framework with three components -- brain (knowledge, memory, reasoning/planning, transferability/generalization), perception (multimodal inputs: text, visual, auditory, etc.), and action (text output, tool use, embodied/physical action); (2) agents in practice -- single-agent scenarios, multi-agent scenarios (cooperative/adversarial), and human-agent cooperation; (3) agent society -- behavior & personality, social environment, emergent social phenomena; plus open problems/future directions. Coverage: ~2023 snapshot (v3 Sep 2023). Reference count: the SCIS journal version (2025) lists 512 references (the arXiv v3 is 86 pages / 12 figures).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (this is a survey, not a benchmark; it constructs no dataset and reports no dataset size or best-system score of its own).
builds_on: Builds conceptually on the classical AI notion of agents (perception-decision-action) and on LLMs as agent foundations; synthesizes prior agent capabilities literature on planning/reasoning (CoT, ReAct, Tree-of-Thoughts-style search), memory (generative-agents-style recency/relevance/importance memory; long-term memory stores incl. databases like ChatDB/DB-GPT), tool use (tool-learning via prompts/demonstrations and feedback), multi-agent systems, and embodied agents. It aggregates and organizes these as a survey rather than extending a single predecessor method.
contrasts_with: Positions itself against task-specific or capability-specific prior agent work (algorithm/training-strategy advances for particular tasks) that lacks a general, powerful foundation model; argues LLM-based agents provide a general starting point. As a survey it contrasts with, and complements, other contemporaneous LLM-agent surveys (e.g., Wang et al. 2023 'A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents') by emphasizing the brain/perception/action framework and agent-society perspective.
lineage: Surveys group: a foundational, broad 2023 survey of LLM-based agents (brain/perception/action; single-/multi-agent; agent society). It is an umbrella reference for the agent-memory, planning, and tool-use sub-topics that the retrieval-augmented-agent lineage (Groups A-F) specializes, rather than a method within any single sub-topic.
